lessons.title: Data Factory vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory

slots.practicalActivity: No Azure resource needed yet: read through Microsoft's Data Factory overview and, for a dataset you pick (e.g. a CSV export plus a SQL table), write down whether moving and shaping it is better suited to ETL or ELT, and whether classic ADF, SSIS, or Fabric Data Factory best fits your hypothetical scenario.
slots.deliverable: A short written note naming your chosen dataset, your ETL-vs-ELT call, and your ADF-vs-SSIS-vs-Fabric recommendation with one sentence of reasoning for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Sign into the Azure portal (a free trial subscription is enough) and provision a real Azure Data Factory instance, then open Data Factory Studio and tour the Author, Monitor, and Manage hubs end to end the way the lesson walks through them.
slots.deliverable: A live, named Data Factory resource in an Azure resource group, plus a written list of what lives under each of the Author, Monitor, and Manage hubs.

lessons.title: Connecting to Azure SQL & On-Premises SQL Server

slots.practicalActivity: In your new Data Factory, create two real linked services: an Azure Blob Storage linked service, testing Account key authentication first and then reconfiguring it to a system-assigned managed identity; and a SQL Server linked service pointed at a SQL Server instance you have access to (e.g. AdventureWorksDW2014 or Northwind). Deliberately mistype the storage account name once to see what a failed Test Connection actually looks like before fixing it.
slots.deliverable: Two working, tested linked services (Blob Storage and SQL Server) visible in the Manage hub, with a written note on what the failed Test Connection error said.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a dataset on top of each linked service from the previous slot, import its schema, then parameterize the Blob Storage dataset's file path so the exact same dataset definition can point at a different file at runtime without being edited.
slots.deliverable: Two datasets (one Blob, one SQL) plus one parameterized dataset whose file-path argument you can change and re-run without touching the dataset itself.

slots.practicalActivity: Build your first real pipeline: drag a Copy activity onto the canvas, wire its source to your SQL dataset and its sink to your Blob Storage dataset, and run it in Debug mode to confirm rows actually land in storage.
slots.deliverable: One working pipeline with a single Copy activity, confirmed successful by a Debug run that lands real rows in Blob Storage.

slots.practicalActivity: Turn on schema drift mapping on your Copy activity's sink and add or remove a column on the source side to watch it propagate. Then add a Lookup activity that reads a small configuration table (e.g. which table name to copy this run) and a Stored Procedure activity that logs the run's completion back into SQL Server.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline demonstrating schema drift handling, plus a Lookup-to-Stored-Procedure chain that logs a completion record to a real SQL table.

lessons.title: Web, Wait, Fail & Set Variable Activities

slots.practicalActivity: Exactly as this lesson lays out, chain Lookup → Copy → Stored Procedure with a Succeeded dependency condition, and add a Fail activity wired to the Copy activity on a Failed condition so the pipeline stops loudly with a clear message on a bad run. Run the whole chain in Debug mode.
slots.deliverable: A three-activity Lookup/Copy/Stored-Procedure pipeline with a Fail-on-failure branch, run successfully end to end in Debug mode.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, build an original end-to-end pipeline against a different table from your SQL source, reusing at least 4 activities from this chapter (Lookup, Copy, Stored Procedure, and Fail, Wait, or Set Variable) chained with dependency conditions you choose yourself.
slots.deliverable: One new, independently built pipeline demonstrating at least 4 chapter-3 activity types with working dependency conditions, confirmed in a Debug run.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a pipeline parameter (e.g. a table name) and a variable to your Chapter 3 pipeline, then wrap the Copy activity in an If Condition checking the parameter and route a second branch through a Switch activity on a different value.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline using one parameter, one variable, an If Condition, and a Switch activity, each tested with at least two different input values.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a ForEach activity that loops over an array of table names (or a Lookup activity's output) and runs a Copy activity once per item. Separately, build an Until activity that polls a condition — using a Wait activity plus a variable increment — until it's met.
slots.deliverable: One pipeline with a working ForEach loop copying multiple tables, and a second pipeline demonstrating an Until loop that terminates correctly.

slots.practicalActivity: Refactor your Chapter 3 pipeline into a reusable child pipeline, then build a new parent pipeline that calls it via Execute Pipeline, passing parameters down. Write 3 original expressions using @pipeline(), @activity(), and a system variable to inspect run metadata at runtime.
slots.deliverable: A parent/child pipeline pair connected by Execute Pipeline, plus 3 original expressions whose output you validated in a Debug run.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: in 45 minutes, design and build one original control-flow pipeline combining at least 4 techniques from this chapter (parameters, ForEach or Until, If Condition or Switch, and Execute Pipeline) with no lesson reference, against a dataset of your choosing.
slots.deliverable: One independently built control-flow pipeline exercising at least 4 chapter-4 techniques, run successfully in Debug mode.

lessons.title: What Is a Mapping Data Flow?

slots.practicalActivity: Create your first mapping data flow, add a Source pointed at one of your real SQL tables, turn on Data Flow Debug mode, and use Data Preview to watch rows actually move through the transformation stream.
slots.deliverable: A new, wired data flow with a live Source connected to real data, confirmed in Debug mode's Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Sink to your data flow writing to Blob Storage or Azure SQL, then insert a Filter transformation (e.g. only rows after a date), a Select transformation dropping unneeded columns, and a Derived Column computing a new field from existing ones.
slots.deliverable: A data flow with Source, Filter, Select, Derived Column, and Sink, producing a correctly filtered and computed output table.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the data flow with a Join transformation combining two of your real tables, an Aggregate transformation summarizing by a grouping column, and a Conditional Split routing rows down two branches by a condition you pick. Then review the data flow's partitioning settings for performance.
slots.deliverable: One data flow exercising Join, Aggregate, and Conditional Split, plus a written note on one performance setting you adjusted and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original mapping data flow from scratch, without lesson guidance, against a different pair of related tables, chaining at least 5 distinct transformations (Source, Filter, Join or Aggregate, Derived Column, Sink) in an order you design yourself.
slots.deliverable: One independently built mapping data flow demonstrating at least 5 chapter-5 transformation types, validated in Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Attach a Schedule trigger to one of your pipelines, configured to run daily at a specific hour with a weekday narrowing, then build a separate Tumbling Window trigger on a different pipeline and compare how its window start/end parameters differ from the Schedule trigger's recurrence.
slots.deliverable: One pipeline with a working Schedule trigger (daily, weekday-restricted) and one with a Tumbling Window trigger, both enabled and visible in the Manage hub.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Event-based (Storage events) trigger that fires when a file lands in your Blob container, confirming it by dropping a real test file in. Then chain two pipelines together using a trigger dependency condition so the second only runs after the first succeeds.
slots.deliverable: A working Storage-event trigger confirmed by a real file drop, plus two pipelines chained by a trigger dependency.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Manage hub, locate the Azure Integration Runtime your pipelines have been using all along, note its region and TTL settings, and read through what each setting actually controls for a real workload.
slots.deliverable: A written note identifying your factory's Azure IR, its region, and one setting you'd change for a production workload, with reasoning.

slots.practicalActivity: If you have a local SQL Server (e.g. the AdventureWorksDW2014 or Northwind instance from Chapter 2), install and register a Self-Hosted Integration Runtime pointing at it; if a real on-prem machine isn't available, write out the exact installation and registration steps instead.
slots.deliverable: A registered Self-Hosted Integration Runtime with a successful connectivity test, or a complete step-by-step installation document if the environment doesn't allow it.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Monitor hub and review your pipeline run history from every previous chapter's pipelines, then configure a retry policy (attempts plus interval) on one activity and set up an Azure Monitor alert rule that fires on pipeline failure.
slots.deliverable: A reviewed run-history list plus one activity with a non-default retry policy and one configured failure alert rule.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break a pipeline (point a Copy activity at a renamed or missing table) to trigger a real failure, apply an error-handling pattern from the lesson so it fails gracefully with a clear message, then wire pipeline diagnostics to a Log Analytics workspace.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline that fails gracefully with a logged, explainable error, with diagnostic logs flowing into Log Analytics.

lessons.title: Dataflow Gen2 vs. Mapping Data Flows

slots.practicalActivity: If you have Fabric trial access, open a Fabric workspace and compare its Data Factory experience side by side with classic ADF Studio; create a Dataflow Gen2 against the same source table you've used all course and compare its authoring experience to your Chapter 5 mapping data flow.
slots.deliverable: A written side-by-side comparison (at least 4 points) between classic ADF and Fabric Data Factory, plus one Dataflow Gen2 built against real data (or a documented walkthrough if Fabric access isn't available).

slots.practicalActivity: Build a simple pipeline inside your Fabric workspace using the same Copy-activity pattern from Chapter 3, landing its output in OneLake instead of Blob Storage, and note which other Fabric items in the same workspace can now see that data directly.
slots.deliverable: A Fabric pipeline landing real data in OneLake, with a written note on what became instantly visible to other Fabric items in the same workspace.

lessons.title: When to Choose ADF vs. Fabric

slots.practicalActivity: Export one of your classic ADF pipelines' ARM template/JSON definition and walk through, step by step, what would need to change to recreate it in Fabric Data Factory. Then write a one-paragraph recommendation for a hypothetical project on when you'd choose ADF versus Fabric Data Factory.
slots.deliverable: A written migration checklist for one real pipeline, plus a one-paragraph ADF-vs-Fabric recommendation with concrete reasoning.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, rebuild one pipeline from an earlier chapter inside Fabric Data Factory from scratch, using Fabric-native equivalents (Dataflow Gen2, OneLake sink) instead of classic ADF components.
slots.deliverable: One pipeline/dataflow pair rebuilt independently inside Fabric, producing the same output as its classic-ADF counterpart.

slots.practicalActivity: Find your Data Factory's system-assigned managed identity Object ID under Properties, grant it a role assignment on your storage account or Key Vault, then rewrite one linked service's password field to reference an Azure Key Vault secret instead of a plain-text credential. Separately, review your factory's RBAC role assignments under Access control (IAM).
slots.deliverable: One linked service now authenticating via a Key Vault reference with no stored password, plus a written RBAC role-assignment review.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect your Data Factory to a Git repository (Azure DevOps or GitHub) under Manage > Git configuration, make a change on a feature branch, and publish it through to a separate Dev/Test ADF instance's ARM template deployment (or document the exact steps if a second environment isn't available).
slots.deliverable: A Git-connected factory with at least one committed feature-branch change, and a documented or completed publish to a second Dev/Test environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Export your factory's full ARM template from the Git-connected branch, then sketch (or build, if you have Azure DevOps access) a release pipeline YAML that deploys that ARM template to a target environment automatically on merge to main.
slots.deliverable: An exported ARM template for your factory plus a written or working Azure DevOps release pipeline definition that deploys it.

slots.practicalActivity: Write out the Northwind Retail capstone scenario in your own words — the on-premises SQL Server source, the 'cleaned up and totaled by region and category' transformation requirement, the unattended-by-8-AM schedule requirement, and the no-plain-text-credentials requirement — then map each one to the specific chapter concept you'll use to satisfy it.
slots.deliverable: A written requirements/traceability table mapping all four Northwind Retail business requirements to the Data Factory concepts (self-hosted IR, mapping data flow, schedule trigger plus error handling, managed identity plus Key Vault) that satisfy them.

lessons.title: Capstone: Connect & Build the Copy Pipeline

slots.practicalActivity: Build the real first stage of the capstone architecture: an integration runtime connection to your on-premises or local SQL Server sales data, and a Copy activity landing it raw into an ADLS Gen2 or Blob Storage 'raw' zone.
slots.deliverable: A working Copy pipeline that reliably lands your real sales source data into a raw storage zone, confirmed in a Debug run.

lessons.title: Capstone: Add Control Flow & Error Handling

slots.practicalActivity: Add control flow and error handling to the capstone pipeline: an If Condition checking the source table exists, a retry policy on the Copy activity for transient failures, and a Fail activity with a clear message if the copy can't complete.
slots.deliverable: The capstone pipeline now surviving, or failing loudly and clearly on, a deliberately simulated missing-table or connection failure.

lessons.title: Capstone: Build the Mapping Data Flow

slots.practicalActivity: Build the capstone's mapping data flow: a Source from your raw zone, a Filter and Derived Column to clean the data, an Aggregate grouping totals by region and product category, and a Sink writing the curated result into an Azure SQL Database 'curated' table.
slots.deliverable: A mapping data flow producing correctly aggregated sales totals by region and category in a real curated SQL table.

slots.practicalActivity: Finish the capstone's operational requirements: attach a Schedule trigger so the whole pipeline runs unattended before 8 AM daily, switch every linked service to a managed identity or Key Vault-referenced credential, and configure an Azure Monitor alert on failure.
slots.deliverable: The capstone pipeline running on an automatic daily schedule, secured with no plain-text credentials, and alerting on failure.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk through the finished Northwind Retail pipeline end to end — source connection, raw copy, control flow and error handling, mapping data flow, schedule, security, and monitoring — as if presenting it to someone who has never seen it, in under 5 minutes, then write down 2 things you'd improve with more time.
slots.deliverable: A completed capstone walkthrough (live or recorded) covering every architecture stage, plus a written list of 2 concrete 'v2' improvements.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design, build, and operationalize real Azure Data Factory pipelines — connecting to on-premises and cloud sources, orchestrating control flow, transforming data visually with mapping data flows, scheduling and securing pipelines with managed identities and Key Vault, and extending the same skills into Microsoft Fabric Data Factory.
